editorial_contributions.text:
The present second edition of this popular book for talented high school students and also for mathematicians contains mostly the material of the first edition. The contents of the first edition is outlined in the report (1991; Zbl 0727.52001).

The second edition is expanded by the following five short chapters. Chapter 5 (five pages) recalls two theorems by \textit{D. Karabash} [Geombinatorics 16, No.~2, 262--265 (2006)] on rectangles that can be tiled by L-tetrominoes of the same orientation in such a way that the tiling has \(2\)-fold symmetry. Chapter 6 (five pages) presents some results on three-dimensional tromino tilings of a cube obtained mostly by \textit{N. Starr} [Geombinatorics 18, No.~2, 72--87 (2008; Zbl 1184.05020)]. Chapter 7 (four pages) comments some results on the Ramsey number \(R(m,n)\), first of all the result by \textit{B. D. McKay} and \textit{S. P. Radziszowski} that \(R(4,5) = 25\) [J. Graph Theory 19, No.~3, 309--322 (1995; Zbl 0822.05050)], and also the estimates \(43 \leq R(5,5) \leq 49\) with the conjecture that \(R(5,5) =43\). See \textit{G. Exoo} [J. Graph Theory 13, No.~1, 97--98 (1989; Zbl 0661.05044)] and \textit{B. D. McKay} and \textit{S. P. Radziszowski} [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. B 69, No.~2, 193--209 (1997; Zbl 0860.05043)].

Chapter 8 (four pages) gives information on the progress in the research on the famous Borsuk problem after the first edition of this book; the story of finding counterexamples. Starting from the well-nown result by \textit{J. Kahn} and \textit{G. Kalai} [Bull. Am. Math. Soc., New Ser. 29, No.~1, 60--62 (1993; Zbl 0786.52002)] and finishing by the result of \textit{A. Hinrichs} and \textit{C. Richter} [Discrete Math. 270, No.~1--3, 137--147 (2003; Zbl 1028.52012)] on the counterexample in \(E^{298}\), which (till now) is the space of the lowest known dimension for which the Borsuk problem has a negative solution. 

Chapter 9 (twelve pages) discusses the following problem of E. Nelson (1950): which is the smallest number \(\chi\) of colours sufficient for colouring the plane in such a way that no two points of the same colour lie apart at unit distance. After recalling the proofs by E. Nelson (1950) and J. Isbell (1950) that \(4 \leq \chi \leq 7\), the author presents results on the \(n\)-colouring of a given type and on the almost chromatic number \(\chi_a\); see the paper by \textit{I. Hoffman} and \textit{A. Soifer} [Geombinatorics 3, No.~2, 38--40 (1993; Zbl 0845.05037)].
